region_3d_semantics_probe.purpose: verify the assignment's stated assumption that window_matrix already encodes the camera lens/sensor-fit FOV in camera view, before relying on it
region_3d_semantics_probe.method: real-window probe scripts (retained at .user/camera-view-probe.py) plus reading the fork source (view3d_navigate_view_camera.cc, view3d_navigate_smoothview.cc, view3d_utils.cc ED_view3d_from_m4, view3d_view.cc view3d_viewmatrix_set/obmat_to_viewmat, blenkernel camera.cc BKE_camera_params_from_view3d/compute_viewplane)
findings: ORBIT convention confirmed by Blender itself: 'Align Camera to View' placed a camera at exactly view_location + view_rotation.to_matrix()@(0,0,view_distance) = (2.090112, -2.511183, 2.348109) -- the existing PERSP conversion is correct and untouched.

Assignment assumption VERIFIED FALSE: in camera view window_matrix[1][1] still carried the passepartout zoom. 50 mm lens, 36 mm sensor, region 1180x2258 (portrait): camera vfov = 39.5978 deg, window_matrix vfov = 71.5078 deg = exactly 2x (BKE_camera_params_from_view3d uses CAMERA_PARAM_ZOOM_INIT_CAMOB/zoom_to_fac(camzoom); default camzoom 0 -> 2.0 zoom-out). Using it would have rendered the passepartout, not the camera frame.
view_camera_sync: rv.view_rotation becomes the camera's world rotation, but rv.view_location and rv.view_distance keep the previous orbit's pivot/distance (stale).
rv.view_camera is None in this fork even inside camera view; the viewed camera is resolved as space.camera (the same v3d->camera the camera view draws through), falling back to scene.camera.

Consequently the CAMERA branch uses the camera object's matrix_world for eye/orientation and view_match.viewport_fov_rad(sensor_width, lens, region aspect) for the FOV -- existing math, reused, not reimplemented.
